Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; can you tell me if these symptoms appeared suddenly or developed gradually over time?

Also, to help narrow this down, have you noticed any trouble with speaking, swallowing, or limb coordination on one specific side of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest is very concerning for Myasthenia Gravis, but the specific trigger of looking up or down also points toward an eye movement issue. Given the combination of ophthalmoparesis and proximal limb weakness, have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis) or difficulty closing your eyes completely?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of fluctuating weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with diplopia, is highly characteristic of Myasthenia Gravis. Your mention of no muscle wasting or weight loss is consistent with this diagnosis, as it helps rule out conditions like motor neuron disease or malignancy. Please confirm if you have noticed any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis) or difficulty swallowing, as these are key confirming symptoms.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
